description: Add authored House sensory, absurdity, and persistent cosmetic-damage interactions without adding globals or replacing canonical puzzle authorities

replacements.new:
<ROUTINE NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS ()
    <COND (<IN? ,LUNCH ,SANDWICH-BAG> <MOVE ,LUNCH ,HERE>)>
    <COND (<IN? ,GARLIC ,SANDWICH-BAG> <MOVE ,GARLIC ,HERE>)>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE NARRATIVE-PHYSICALITY-HOOK ()
    <COND
      (<AND <VERB? PUT> <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,SANDWICH-BAG> <FSET? ,SANDWICH-BAG ,RMUNGBIT>>
       <TELL "The brown sack will still surround an object in a philosophical sense, but the torn seam makes it a poor container." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <VERB? THROW> ,PRSI <OR <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,FRONT-DOOR> <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,BOARDED-WINDOW>>>
       <COND (<MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSO>
              <FSET ,PRSI ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSO " strikes the boarding with a hard wooden report. One weathered surface is newly scarred, but the boards and their fasteners remain very much in charge of the entrance." CR>)
             (T
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSO " thumps against the boarding and drops away. The house declines to reinterpret this as a key." CR>)>
       <MOVE ,PRSO ,HERE>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<EQUAL? ,PRSO ,WHITE-HOUSE>
       <COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
              <COND (<FSET? ,WHITE-HOUSE ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The once-imposing white colonial house now bears a few fresh scars in its painted siding. It remains large, wealthy-looking, and inconveniently house-shaped." CR>)
                    (T
                     <TELL "The white colonial house is substantial rather than picturesque at close range: painted siding, boarded openings, a chimney, and the quiet confidence of architecture that expects you to use doors." CR>)>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? TAKE>
              <TELL "You get both hands on the house. The house, having foundations and several rooms, wins immediately." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? TOUCH>
              <TELL "The painted siding is cool, slightly chalky, and much less abstract under your fingertips." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? SMELL>
              <TELL "Old paint, dry wood, grass, and the faint mineral smell of masonry: a house, convincingly enough." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? LISTEN>
              <TELL "The house contributes creaks, settling wood, and a silence too large to be reassuring." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? KICK>
              <TELL "You kick the house. The siding answers with a flat thump; your foot supplies the more detailed commentary." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<AND <VERB? MUNG CUT ATTACK> ,PRSI <MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSI>>
              <FSET ,WHITE-HOUSE ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " bites into the painted exterior and leaves an ugly scar. This is damage, not progress; the house remains a house and the canonical entrances remain authoritative." CR>
              <RTRUE>)>)
      (<OR <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,FRONT-DOOR> <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,BOARDED-WINDOW>>
       <COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
              <COND (<FSET? ,PRSO ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The weathered boards show fresh dents, cuts, and bruised grain. Their nails are still sunk deep and the barrier remains structurally effective." CR>)
                    (T
                     <TELL "Weathered boards cross the opening in a deliberately joyless arrangement. The wood is old; the fasteners are not casually loose." CR>)>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? TOUCH>
              <TELL "The boards are dry and rough. Nail heads sit nearly flush with the wood, offering little purchase to bare fingers." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? LISTEN>
              <TELL "A knock produces the hollow report of wood backed by a much larger empty house." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? KICK>
              <FSET ,PRSO ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The boards jump in their fastenings with a violent crack and settle back into place. You have offended the lumber without solving the problem." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<AND <VERB? MUNG CUT ATTACK> ,PRSI <MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSI>>
              <FSET ,PRSO ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " tears at the weathered surface and raises splinters, but the fastening pattern keeps the barrier intact. A damaged board is not automatically a useful doorway." CR>
              <RTRUE>)>)
      (<EQUAL? ,PRSO ,KITCHEN-TABLE>
       <COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
              <COND (<FSET? ,KITCHEN-TABLE ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The kitchen table is sturdy, scarred, and now newly gouged. Old preparation marks and your recent contribution compete for space on the wood." CR>)
                    (T
                     <TELL "The kitchen table is heavy wood, marked by recent food preparation: faint knife tracks, crumbs, and the displaced order of somebody who expected to return." CR>)>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? TOUCH>
              <TELL "The tabletop is dry, solid, and faintly rough where years of use have worn through its finish." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? SMELL>
              <TELL "Wood, stale crumbs, and the lingering sharpness of food prepared not terribly long ago." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? KICK>
              <FSET ,KITCHEN-TABLE ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The table shudders, its contents rattle, and a fresh scuff appears low on one leg. It remains stubbornly table-shaped." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<AND <VERB? MUNG CUT ATTACK> ,PRSI <MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSI>>
              <FSET ,KITCHEN-TABLE ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " chews a fresh gouge into the wood. The table absorbs the abuse and remains a perfectly serviceable surface, though less eligible for resale." CR>
              <RTRUE>)>)
      (<EQUAL? ,PRSO ,SANDWICH-BAG>
       <COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
              <COND (<FSET? ,SANDWICH-BAG ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The brown sack still smells fiercely of hot peppers, but one seam has been cut open. It can be carried; trusting it with small valuables would be optimism." CR>)
                    (T
                     <TELL "The elongated brown sack is thin, flexible paper or fiber, creased from use and saturated with the unmistakable smell of hot peppers." CR>)>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? TOUCH>
              <TELL "The sack crackles softly under your fingers. Its material is thin enough to fold, tear, soak, and generally suffer from ambitious ownership." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? SMELL>
              <TELL "Hot peppers dominate completely. Whatever else the sack has experienced has wisely declined to compete." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<AND <VERB? CUT MUNG> ,PRSI <MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSI>>
              <COND (<FSET? ,SANDWICH-BAG ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The sack is already split along one seam. Further surgery would mostly produce smaller and less useful sack." CR>)
                    (T
                     <FSET ,SANDWICH-BAG ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS>
                     <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " opens a ragged seam in the brown sack. Anything loose inside tumbles out; the sack remains one object, but it has retired from dependable container service." CR>)>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<AND <VERB? SHAKE> <FSET? ,SANDWICH-BAG ,RMUNGBIT>>
              <NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS>
              <TELL "You shake the torn sack. Anything that could still pretend to be contained stops pretending." CR>
              <RTRUE>)>)
      (<EQUAL? ,PRSO ,RUG>
       <COND (<VERB? EXAMINE>
              <COND (<FSET? ,RUG ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The large oriental rug is heavy, dusty, and now visibly frayed along one abused edge. None of this makes the thing meaningfully lighter." CR>)
                    (T
                     <TELL "The oriental rug is thick, old, and extremely heavy. Dust lives deep in the pile, and the weave is dense enough to explain why moving it is work." CR>)>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? TOUCH>
              <TELL "The pile is coarse with age and dust; beneath it is a dense backing with surprising weight." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? SMELL>
              <TELL "Dust, old fibers, and the dry enclosed smell of a room that has kept its secrets under furniture." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? KICK>
              <TELL "Your kick raises a small cloud of dust and accomplishes approximately nothing against the rug's mass." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<AND <VERB? CUT MUNG> ,PRSI <MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSI>>
              <FSET ,RUG ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " parts some of the dense outer fibers and leaves a ragged edge. The rug is damaged, not transformed into a convenient trap-door solution." CR>
              <RTRUE>)>)
      (<EQUAL? ,PRSO ,KITCHEN-WINDOW>
       <COND (<VERB? TOUCH>
              <TELL "The frame is painted wood; the pane is cool glass held in an old, slightly stubborn sash." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? LISTEN>
              <TELL "Through the window comes the faint outdoor hush of grass and forest. The frame itself offers an occasional dry creak." CR>
              <RTRUE>)
             (<VERB? SMELL>
              <TELL "Old wood and outdoor air. Windows are not celebrated for their bouquet." CR>
              <RTRUE>)>)>
    <RFALSE>>

<ROUTINE MATERIAL-TOOL-CLEAN? (OBJ)
